correctness.rationale: For every integer g>=3 and k>=1, n in E1 requires n=1+b with b in the odd- or even-supported digit class. In odd class the nonoverlapping mixed sum forces 1; an even+even representation is possible exactly when all odd-position digits of b are <=1, by carrying one from each adjacent even digit, with both summands positive. For even class splitting base-g columns classifies 2,3 and 1+g^{2j} (j>=1) as unique essential cases; g=3 and carry boundary handled explicitly. Thus the three stated families are disjoint and the odd-digit family has g^k-2^k vectors, plus k-1 powers and 2 exceptions, proving exact count g^k-2^k+k+1 for all g,k. Independent code enumerates all admissible positive summands and ALL unordered representations below g^{2k}, checking equality of full essentiality sets (not just totals) for (g,k)=(3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(4,2),(5,2),(6,2), giving counts 3,8,23,15,24,35. Finite checks supplement unlimited carry proof.
